title: Causa Justa road-closure protests in Colón
location: Colón province: downtown streets 16, 5 and 3; Arco Iris; El Nazareno; La Verbena; and Panama–Colón highway near Puerto Escondido
scope: Multiple locations in Colón province reported on the same morning; organization/coordination across sites not yet independently established.
organizer: Movimiento Causa Justa; article also reports Suntracs members participated. Article identifies the movement as directed by Parlacen deputy Carlos Biby Outten.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending: the article reports groups of demonstrators but no attendee count. 'Dozens of drivers' refers to motorists trapped in traffic, not protesters. No >=50 threshold can be established from this source.

start_date.summary: The article dates the closures and police response to Monday, 18 January 2021.

location.summary: The article names several streets and neighborhoods in Colón and the Panama–Colón highway near Puerto Escondido.

organizer.summary: The article attributes the action to Causa Justa and reports Suntracs members participated; it names Carlos Biby Outten as movement director.

demands.summary: The article identifies job positions, better living conditions, economic reactivation, drinking water and other provincial social problems as demands; Causa Justa submitted a 15-item petition to the government.

participants_original.summary: The article says groups of demonstrators and separately says dozens of drivers were trapped, but publishes no demonstrator estimate.

state_response.arrests.summary: The National Police reportedly said it detained about 15 people, including seven women.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The article reports a crowd-control police unit intervened to reopen Calle 16, Barrio Norte and Barrio Sur.

notes: A distinct local action is plausible, but the article reports several sites and a multi-item petition without establishing whether there was one coordinated province-wide action or separate local gatherings. Suntracs participation concerning pension dialogue may represent a distinct demand. Evidence of tire burning and barricades is reported, but this alone does not resolve the protester-violence code. Do not treat the governor's characterization as verified conduct.
open_questions: Was there one coordinated Causa Justa action across sites or several separate gatherings?
Was any demonstrator attendance estimate or clear >=50 description published?
When did the road closures end, and did the same mobilization continue into another date or month?
What was the relationship between Causa Justa's petition and Suntracs' opposition to pension dialogue?
Were any other state response actions reported beyond arrests and reopening roads?

title: Causa Justa protest at the DAS office and Panama Port in Colón
location: Colón province, including Plaza Millenium (Dirección de Asuntos Sociales office) and Panama Port freight area
scope: Reported local protest at two sites in Colón; sequence between the DAS office and port is described, but whether other groups/sites were involved is unknown.
organizer: Members of Movimiento Causa Justa; article names Parlacen deputy Carlos Outten among those arrested.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending: the article reports at least 12 arrests, not total attendance. It provides no count or qualitative description establishing 50 or more demonstrators.

start_date.summary: La Prensa dates the protest to Thursday, January 21, 2021.

location.summary: The article places the group at the DAS office at Plaza Millenium, then Panama Port's freight area.

organizer.summary: The article identifies participants as members of Movimiento Causa Justa and names Carlos Outten.

demands.summary: The article states demands for jobs and economic reactivation.

participants_original.summary: No demonstrator attendance number appears; at least 12 people were arrested, which is not a crowd size.

state_response.arrests.summary: The article reports at least 12 arrests, including Carlos Outten.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The article says police intervened after participants entered Panama Port's freight area but does not say they moved participants or broke up the protest.

state_response.police_force.summary: La Prensa reports that Outten received an electrical discharge from a police officer using a Taser pistol and was taken for medical attention. Actual discharge/use is documented; the article does not say whether the officer separately aimed before firing or specify a particular injury.

state_response.beatings.summary: The source documents Taser use that delivered an electrical discharge to Carlos Outten, but does not describe a separate beating, specify an injury, or classify the Taser use under the original beating category; mapping remains unresolved.

notes: A separate physical action on January 21 is reported three days after the January 18 multi-site Causa Justa closures. Available sources show the same movement returned on February 18, but no evidence of continuous occupation from January 18 to January 21 or into February. Do not merge solely because the organizer and general employment demands recur. La Prensa reports that a police officer used a Taser pistol to deliver an electrical discharge to Carlos Outten, who was taken for medical attention. A specific injury is not documented; separate aiming is not described. This is not evidence of firearm shooting or a separate beating. The report says police intervened at the port but does not specify dispersal.
open_questions: Was attendance at least 50?
Does the additional coding procedure distinguish Taser/electroshock from beatings or other police force?
Was the January 21 gathering a distinct episode from the January 18 action under the original episode rule?
When did the January 21 action physically end?
Were any demands accommodated through documented government reception or negotiation?
